_about: How each meaning becomes Kutchi words: slots, agreement, register variants, exceptions (engine-design § 5.4). Built by build/lang/import_all.mjs.

Item.src: grammar-notes §2, §4 (hakro ambo, ba amba), §40 (wadho chokro), §41 (wadhe chokre sathe)

Of.src: grammar-notes §47 (agrees with the thing owned), §48 (owner takes -e), §49 (je before a postposition); decision 30 (b), (c)

MixedIn.src: grammar-notes §6 (dudh waari chai: said of chai only)

exceptions.what: a counted thing in chai (not '{x} waari chai')
exceptions.src: grammar-notes §6 (two sugars is not ba khun waari chai: Muke chai me ba khun khapeti)

Without.src: grammar-notes §10 (dudh wagar ji chai); whether ji agrees with the dish is open (dungri wagar ji daar, daar's gender unknown: L36)

WithFood.what: with, joining an extra to food

PredDat.src: grammar-notes §1 (muke hakri maani khape / khapeti; muke ba amba khapanta), §31

IsA.src: grammar-notes §42 C33-C35 (Chokro wadho ai. Chokra wadha ain.), §44 C42

BelongsTo.src: grammar-notes §50 C60 (Nana jo ai: an unknown thing takes the he-form); decision 30 (f)

Say.src: a fixed phrase said on its own (grammar-kb feature 29)

And.src: grammar-notes §6 (ne chai, ne dudh: a list takes ne before each item)

Then.src: grammar-notes §7 (ne poi = and then, confirmed), §24 B12

First.src: grammar-notes §7 (Muke pela daar khape, ne poi maani); pela alone is a draft in data/cook.json

NoItem.src: grammar-notes §11 (khun na), §13 (laal na), §24 B1; Mum called the short form very informal (lexicon §2 doubt 1)
notes: The polite whole sentence is NotNeed (Muke {x} nati khape). A hidden 'no' row is two words so it does not stand out by length (docs/archive/language/cook-word-changes-B.md §2).

Only.src: grammar-notes §25 B13 (kali amba: the same for he- and she-words)

Now.src: grammar-notes §25 B14 (hane = now in a sequence of cooking steps)
notes: hever (now, in general) is the urgent one: hever kadh! (§29 R6, §37.6). Not used for steps.

GiveMe.src: grammar-notes §9 (Muke chamchi de; pass is the same as give); data/cook.json lines.give still marks it draft
notes: Mum said Muke chamchi de (§9), so the draft flag in data/cook.json may be stale: Zafar to say (clash list).

For.src: grammar-notes §8 (Hi Nana lai ai: lai = for)

CanYouMake.src: grammar-notes §27 B40 (Tu muke chai banai dinda? / Aai muke chai banai dinda?), §30 K7-K9, §29 R10
notes: No word for 'can': the question is in the rising voice at the end (§27 B40). dinda and dinde: which is for an elder is open (§37.7).

HowAreYou.src: grammar-notes §21 (Tu ki aiye? to a child; Aai ki aayo? to an elder), §27 B43

ImFine.src: grammar-notes §27 B43, §29 R11 (Aau theek ai; spelling confirmed by Zafar 26 Sept)
notes: Mum says ai, not aiya, here (Aau theek ai) although 'I am' elsewhere is aiya (Aau rasore me aiya, §51): a fixed phrase or a real difference? Ask Mum.

NotNeed.src: grammar-notes §11 (muke khun nati khape; informally khun nati khape), §24 B1 (muke nato khape: nato he, nati she)
notes: A bare na is rude when turning something down (§11, rule G7): the polite no is the phrase na, muke na khape. Very informally just khun na (NoItem).

Where.src: grammar-notes §30 K12 (Chamchi kida ai? Cup kida ai?: the word order is right), §23 (kida ai?)

LocatedAt.src: grammar-notes §15 (cup table je mathe ai), §18 (the noun doesn't change before je, -o words take -e: darwaje je puthiya), §36 C14

LocatedAtShort.src: grammar-notes §15 (the everyday, shorter version drops je: cup table mathe ai)

Command.src: grammar-notes §38 (the bare commands to a child: atto gund, samosa waar, samosa tar, chulo bar, paani bhari chad), §12

exceptions.what: a command to an elder (Mum has said only the bare command to a child)
exceptions.src: grammar-notes §38 (polite and 'for me' forms are still unknown), For Mum next time 11

DoIt.src: grammar-notes §38 I4, I5, I11, I13, I16 (wiji chad, kadhi chad, kapi chad, bego kari chad, paani bhari chad: chad = leave it, finish it)

exceptions.what: a 'put it in' command to an elder

Dont.src: grammar-notes §12 (na next to the verb, after it: khun na wij, khun na wapur, ad na, hal na, bol na, watu na kar)
notes: na before the verb is urgent or changes the meaning: see DontNow (§12).

DontNow.src: grammar-notes §12 (na ad is the sharp warning: it's hot, you'll burn!)

Point.src: grammar-notes §43 C36 (hi wadho chokro, hu wadho chokro: you either point or the describing word goes with a verb), §13

PossPron.src: grammar-notes §54 C72-C78 (munjo cup, munji kursi, munja amba), §55 C79 (munje cup me, toje ambe mathe)
notes: The ending follows the thing owned, not the owner (§54). The plural -yu on the thing is dropped when something else shows 'more than one' (hi mare munji kursi ain).

Most.src: grammar-notes §43 (wadho ma wadho, nindho ma nindho: the biggest, the smallest)
notes: Heard only with the he-forms of big and small; the she-form is not said.

Unit.src: grammar-notes §25 (hakri lakri mishkaki, ba lakri mishkaki), §29 R7; data/cook.json ph-lakri: with gos, boga and mixed it is Claude's extension, to check

exceptions.src: grammar-notes §25, §29 R7 (hakri lakri mishkaki: Mum said it with mishkaki)

notes: Another way Mum said it: mishkaki ji lakri, kebab ji lakri (a skewer of …, §39 I28). Which one the game uses: to decide.

Amt.src: grammar-notes §24 B4-B5 (adh, aako said on their own: Ne adh, Ne aako)

Exclaim.src: a fixed phrase said with force (grammar-kb feature 29)

Ask.src: a fixed phrase said as a question (grammar-kb feature 29)

WantIn.src: grammar-notes §6 (Muke chai me ba khun khapeti: in my tea I want two sugars; khape is the informal ending the game uses); data/cook.json lines.sugar (draft)
notes: Mum's own sentence was the polite one, with khapeti after ba khun (two sugars): a she-singular ending on a count of two, unexplained until the gender of khun is settled (L34).

exceptions.what: the polite 'in my chai I want two sugars' (Mum said khapeti with ba khun)

OnShort.src: grammar-notes §55 C79 (toje ambe mathe, toji kursi mathe: the short postposition sits straight after the noun; the fuller one adds je, §15)

Place.src: grammar-notes §15 (cup kabaat je andar, table je niche, darwaje je puthiya: the place belongs to the thing), §18, §49 (Nani je ambe je mathe; Nana je cup je andar)

Lift.src: grammar-notes §25 B15 (inke hane kadh: lift it out now); data/cook.json lines.lift names the thing where Mum said inke (it): Claude's extension, to check
notes: hever kadh is the urgent one (§29 R6, §37.6); hane kadh is the gentle one in a sequence of steps (Cook keeps hane kadh).

Leave.src: grammar-notes §25 B16 (inke chadi de: leave it be); data/cook.json lines.leave names the thing where Mum said inke (it): Claude's extension, to check

FirstThen.src: grammar-notes §7 (Muke pela daar khape, ne poi maani: pela X, ne poi Y); pela is a draft in data/cook.json
notes: Three steps (pela X, ne poi Y, ne poi Z) are not Mum's own sentence: only two steps were said.

NeedFirstThen.src: grammar-notes §7 (Muke pela daar khape, ne poi maani: Mum's own sentence); pela is a draft in data/cook.json

AndKind.what: joining a second kind of the same dish ('and one with potato')

Times.src: data/clinic/lang.json lines.times (no Kutchi: gap Times); Round 5 L54

Fetch.what: Nani sending the child to fetch a list ('bring me flour, sugar and milk')
